name: Bound the reconcile verifier's work to the job's pg-boss expiry
description:
A reconcile round can run several times longer than the expiry of the job it runs in, so pg-boss redelivers the job while its first handler is still working. Raised by Copilot on PR 70 (thread `r4093949560`), which changed `RECONCILE_VERIFY_MAX` from 20 to 40. The mechanism is real and was verified from source, but it is **not** introduced by that PR — it is on master today and the cap change widens it. PR 70 therefore corrects the comment that described the sizing wrongly and leaves the behaviour alone; this ticket is the behaviour.

## The mechanism

`RECONCILE_QUEUE` is created through `createEngineQueue` (`apps/worker/src/index.ts`), which sets `expireInSeconds = engineTimeoutMs + 5 min` — 15 minutes at the default `ENGINE_TIMEOUT_MS` of 600000. That sizing is for **one** engine call.

`runVerifier` (`apps/worker/src/jobs/reconcile-findings.ts`) does not make one call. It iterates `selection.chunks` and awaits `engine.complete` inside the loop, serially, one sandboxed container per chunk. Each call goes through `runEngineCli` without a `timeoutMs`, so `engine-sandbox.ts` gives it the full `engineTimeoutMs` — checked for `claude-engine.ts`, `codex-engine.ts` and `opencode-engine.ts`, so it holds for every provider. There is no `AbortSignal` and no deadline over the round, so the call durations simply add up.

**There is also no early abort.** The `try/catch` in that loop wraps a single chunk: a call that throws or times out is caught, its candidates are recorded unanswered, and the loop moves to the next chunk. A provider outage therefore does not end the round early — it makes the round as long as it can possibly be.

Chunk counts, recomputed from `MAX_CHARS_PER_CALL = 24_000` and the packing loop in `selectVerifyCandidates`, at the ~3 kB per candidate the docblock assumes: a cap of 20 is three calls, a cap of 40 is five. So the pathological round goes from ~30 minutes to ~50 against a 15-minute expiry. The expiry was already breachable at two chunks, which is why this is a pre-existing defect rather than a regression — but the realistic round is what actually changes. At a plausible 2–3 minutes per call, three calls sit comfortably inside the 15 minutes and five sit on the edge.

## What it costs

pg-boss redelivers the expired job while the original handler keeps running. The round is idempotent — `createOutboundMessage` is `onConflictDoNothing` on a unique `idempotencyKey`, so no second outbound row appears — so the damage is not to the data. It is:

- the verifier paid for twice, and `runVerifier` calls `engine.complete` without `maxBudgetUsd` (only the review path passes one), so the bucket cap is the round's only spending bound;
- the queue's single `retryLimit: 1` spent on a job that never failed, so a genuine GitHub failure on the redelivered run leaves that head with no reconcile at all;
- a wider window on the head-currency guard, which is read once near the start of the job and never re-checked. Pre-existing and knowingly accepted under R9 in the plan, but a longer round widens the race.

## Fix

**Not** what the review literally asks for — sizing the expiry for the verifier's maximum number of chunks. That maximum is the cap itself: the `chunk.length > 0` guard deliberately lets one oversized candidate occupy a call alone, so 40 buckets can be 40 chunks, and an expiry sized for that would be over six hours. A stuck job holding its slot that long is worse than what we have.

Take the other half of the sentence instead and **bound the work**. Give `runVerifier` a wall-clock deadline derived from the queue's expiry and stop starting a new chunk once the remaining budget cannot cover another `engineTimeoutMs`. The buckets not asked about degrade to "still open" and get logged — which is already exactly what happens to buckets cut by the cap (`"reconcile: verifier budget exhausted; the rest persist unverified"`), so this needs no new semantics, no new column and no migration; it reuses a degradation path the feature already defines and the console already renders.

Worth doing in the same pass: the `carried_over` panel and the logs should let an operator tell a bucket cut by the cap from one cut by the clock, since the two mean different things about whether asking again would help.

Estimate: half a day to a day, most of it the test that drives the loop past the deadline and asserts the remaining buckets persist unverified rather than being lost or answered.

**Done when:** a reconcile round cannot outlive the expiry of the job it runs in; buckets dropped for time degrade to "still open" on the same path as buckets dropped by the cap, and are distinguishable from them in the log; and the `RECONCILE_QUEUE` comment in `apps/worker/src/index.ts` describes whatever sizing rule the fix settles on.
